chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he was asked about a man: is it proper for him to perform salat while his wife is performing salat in front of him? He said:

He should not perform salat until he places between himself and her more than ten cubits. If she is on his right or his left, he should place between himself and her the like of that. If she is performing salat behind him, then there is no harm, even if she touches his garment. And if the woman is sitting, lying down, or standing without being in salat, then there is no harm wherever she may be.

Thus, the proper way regarding this report is that we understand it as indicating a form of recommendation. It is also possible that the consideration of ten cubits between them applies only when they are on a single line; but if the man is ahead of her, even by a handspan, then this consideration falls away, according to what he detailed in the earlier reports.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman in relation to prayer placement
key_terms.بِشِبْرٍ: by a handspan, indicating slight precedence
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَذْرُعٍ: ten cubits as a measure of separation
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or objection

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman performs salat beside or in front of a man during salat?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of a man and a woman performing salat in close proximity. It indicates a recommended separation in certain arrangements, while clarifying that no issue exists if the woman is behind him or not herself engaged in salat, and the closing explanation frames the distance requirement as one of istihbab rather than strict obligation.
